evals.prompt: The Umbraco MCP is connected to our Umbraco 17 site; this session can't call it, so evals/files/mcp/site-context.md has what the read tools returned. Treat it as the live site. Add authors, and put the Authors folder under the Home Page so it's with everything else. Then swap the article's Author Name field for a picker.
evals.expected_output: The agent specifies authorFolder and author in Data/, with the folder allowed at root (not under the home page, with the reason), the item not at root, the folder allowing the item and the item allowing nothing, and neither with a template or compositions. It adds a multinode tree picker data type restricted to author, maximum 1, used by a new property on articlePage, and keeps authorName because replacing it would lose 300 typed names without a migration. expectations: Requirements pages exist under docs/umbraco-schema/Document-Types/Data/ for a folder type `authorFolder` and an item type `author`
`authorFolder` has Allowed at root Yes and the agent explains why it sits at the content root rather than under the home page; `author` has Allowed at root No
`authorFolder` allows `author` as a child; `author` has Allowed children —; neither has a default template or compositions

A picker data type requirements doc exists under docs/umbraco-schema/Data-Types/ using `Umbraco.MultiNodeTreePicker`, restricted to the `author` type with a maximum of 1, and articlePage gains a new property using it (Update page or checklist item)
The agent does not delete or convert `authorName` in this change, and says moving the 300 typed names to author items is a content migration
Every requirements page and the changeset have the status `proposed`; the agent stops for approval and does not claim anything was created or verified on the site

evals.prompt: Umbraco 17, no MCP on this machine and the site isn't running, so go on what I tell you. We have Article Page (articlePage) and News Page (newsPage), both using SEO Composition (seoComposition), and a Home Page (homePage) allowed at root. We want to tag articles and news with topics; editors currently use the built-in Tags editor and keep inventing duplicates like 'Finance' and 'finance'. Each topic needs a short description and an icon, and some topics sit under broader themes. To save time later, please make one generic Taxonomy Item type with a Type dropdown (topic, region, sector) that we can reuse for every list. Requirements docs go in docs/umbraco-schema/ (only a README there). Write it up with the backoffice steps.
evals.expected_output: The agent specifies a topic folder and topic item in Data/ rather than a generic taxonomyItem with a Type field, and explains why each list gets its own folder and item. It chooses data items over the Tags editor because of the duplicates and per-topic fields. Themes are handled by letting the folder allow itself, or an explicit departure is flagged. A picker restricted to topics goes on a composition shared by articles and news (or both types). Existing types are the user's word; the apply is a manual walkthrough after approval; nothing is claimed as done.
expectations: The requirements doc defines a dedicated folder and item for topics (e.g. `topicFolder` and `topic`) under docs/umbraco-schema/Document-Types/Data/, not a generic `taxonomyItem` with a type dropdown, and the agent explains why
The agent recommends data items over the Tags editor, citing the duplicates or the per-topic description and icon
Broader themes are handled by letting the folder allow itself (sub-folders), or the agent explicitly flags that making topics parents of topics departs from the convention
A picker data type requirements doc restricted to the topic item type exists, and the picker property is placed on a composition shared by articlePage and newsPage or on both types

Existing types are flagged Exists or named as plain text on the user's word and the agent says they were not read from the site; it says the apply is a manual backoffice walkthrough and produces no uSync, package.xml or C# files

Every requirements page and the changeset have the status `proposed`; the agent asks for approval and does not claim anything was created or verified; if it did not run lint-requirements.mjs it says the requirements doc was not linted
